text:
Recent work distinguishes recurring interests from immediate intent. [HyperHawkes (2025)](https://evazangerle.at/publication/peintner-www-2025/) combines repeated intent dynamics with short-term adaptation; [MgRIA (2026)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1567422326000037) models multiple repurchase cycles. Conversely, [Learning to Forget (2026 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12714) treats some purchases as intent completion, motivating checks for post-purchase redundancy. These support separate diagnostic hypotheses: recent-history alignment, recurring-theme support across separated periods, and similarity to recently acquired items. History alone cannot establish current need, ownership, or saturation; unseen-item filtering also means redundancy probes must examine similar substitutes rather than exact repeats.

Compatibility requires explicit evidence. A [2024 product-matching study](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44163-024-00159-8) reports difficulty with model numbers and fine specifications. For this task, code compatibility as supported, contradicted, or unknown using only titles/descriptions and identifiable history links; missing specifications remain unknown. [Uncertainty-based abstention research (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.10960) supports withholding unsupported claims, although its evidence concerns LLM reliability rather than recommendation ranking. Abstain from compatibility judgments without removing required recommendations or changing evaluation.

Proposed feedback validation: audit all twenty training-user lists with a shared codebook covering temporal relevance, recurring-interest evidence, possible purchase completion, explicit incompatibility, and insufficient evidence. Attach source snippets and timestamps to each judgment; independently double-code examples, report agreement and disagreements, and retain unknowns. Treat simulator feedback as hypotheses rather than verified preferences; infer no diversity/conformity traits. Keep these qualitative diagnostics separate from the selection objective: macro-average validation HR@10 across all four categories.
